task_instance: De novo protein backbone design: call the RFDiffusion NIM with the skill's dummy input PDB, contigs="80-120", diffusion_steps=50, and save the returned output_pdb as designed_backbone.pdb.
blocker_detail: The core deliverable is a model-generated protein backbone PDB produced by the RFDiffusion NIM, which is only reachable by executing code: either a Python requests HTTP POST to the hosted NVIDIA inference endpoint, or a local Docker container with an NVIDIA GPU. The office-assistant runtime cannot run code, shell commands, or Docker, so the request can be written as text (request_denovo.py) but never executed. The model itself cannot be reproduced by hand: a diffusion model generates the 3D backbone coordinates, so writing a plausible PDB would be fabricating the deliverable. Compounding this, the skill's endpoints are redacted placeholders, hosted access requires an NGC API key (credentials), and the runtime round also forbids web fetch/search; but the primary, unavoidable blocker is the inability to run any code to invoke the model.
evidence: Read SKILL.md (bionemo-rfdiffusion-nim). Chose minimal de novo case per the skill's Request Pattern. Created sample input input_dummy.pdb (the skill's DUMMY_PDB) and wrote the exact request script request_denovo.py in the work directory. Could not execute it: no shell/code-execution tool exists in this runtime, so no POST to the NIM endpoint and no local Docker run is possible, and result["output_pdb"] (the designed backbone) is never obtained. No designed_backbone.pdb was produced; fabricating coordinates would misrepresent the model output, so it was not done.
